newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet amends banking guarantee fund law.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet amends banking guarantee fund law.

text.p: The Polish government said on Tuesday it had amended a law on the banking guarantee fund (BFG) by giving it access to more information on ailing banks and increased its guarantees for individual savers' deposits.
"The draft provides for increasing the guaranteed sum from 3,000 Ecus and 4,000 Ecus," the government said in a statement.
The statement also said that amendments, which will have to clear parliament and be signed by the president, also provided for better cooperation between the BFG and administrators of bankrupt banks.
"The BFG should be informed fast enough about launching bankruptcy procedures and should take part in the procedures," it said.

The statement did not say whether the government approved or rejected an earlier proposal that would allow the BFG to have access to information protected by the banking secrecy rules. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
